description: Per-edge custom cell borders on an editable KPI scorecard in the Svelte 5 data grid. It opens like a sheet with a 1 to 1000 row gutter and A to Z column letters, and spreadsheetLayout paints each border through an absolutely positioned overlay inside the cell so there are no border-collapse conflicts. Edit any plan or actual cell and the subtotals and borders re-derive: green double for beating target, blue solid for hitting it, amber dotted for a near miss, red dashed for a bad miss, and a coloured full frame for the row champion.

faq.question: How are per-edge borders specified?
faq.answer: As CellBorderSpec entries in the spreadsheetLayout prop, each naming a cell and the top, right, bottom or left style. The layout is a $derived of the data, so editing a value changes the specs and the overlay repaints.

faq.question: Why an overlay instead of CSS borders on the cell?
faq.answer: Adjacent cells share edges, so a double border on one and a dashed one on its neighbour fight under border-collapse. An overlay div per cell draws exactly what the spec says without affecting layout.

faq.question: Does this work with virtualization?
faq.answer: Yes. Row and column virtualization are both on in this demo; the overlay is part of the cell, so it is created and recycled with it.
